description: Country-by-country game recommendations for police training and recruitment capability levels. These are derived model recommendations, not a claim about any country's official police academy, recruitment rank, staffing roster, or legal requirements.

methodology.recruitment: round(1 + 4×modeledStaffingGap + 0.025×economyCapacityIndex + 2.5×populationScale + 0.01×urbanComplexityIndex); clamp 1–10. Population scale is log-normalized to [0,1].
caveats: No universal international numeric police-training or recruitment-level scale exists for all countries.
Country-specific national law, police academy curricula, approved establishment sizes and recruitment rules were not available in a harmonized 249-country dataset.

Levels are strategy-game estimates from the project's existing baseline/context fields. Inputs with modelled or fallback provenance remain modelled; level recommendations do not become official facts.
The international references inform training quality, human rights, ethics, oversight, evaluation and capacity-building considerations; they do not prescribe these country-level numbers.

sources.title: United Nations Police: Guidelines on police capacity building and development
sources.usedFor: Capacity-building areas, training objectives, monitoring, advising, material support and accountability.

sources.title: OSCE/ODIHR: Guidelines on Human Rights Education for Law Enforcement Officials
sources.usedFor: Curricula, core competencies, evaluation, professional development and human-rights education.

sources.title: UNODC: Handbook on Police Accountability, Oversight and Integrity
sources.usedFor: Recruitment, training, professional integrity, supervision, audits and accountability.

sources.title: World Bank population indicator SP.POP.TOTL
sources.usedFor: Population context when the existing source row contains an observation.

methodology.editable: Additive versioned JSON asset. Change any recommended level or model input here; the UI labels the values as model recommendations and never reclassifies them as official country rules.
